symptom: An inherited Array.prototype index-zero setter can intercept indexed validation-error writes, leaving an invalid Outcome Ledger record with an empty error array. An inherited index-17 setter can drop the last canonical evidence digest, causing distinct valid records to hash identically and potentially be classified IDEMPOTENT_NOOP rather than CONFLICT. Both are synthetic runtime conditions; no production or real settlement evidence was affected.
lesson: Replacing Array.prototype.push with errors[errors.length] still leaves a validation sink vulnerable to inherited numeric setters; likewise descriptor-safe reads cannot protect canonical hashes when output arrays are populated through inherited-setter-sensitive assignment. This is the same previously learned ambient prototype boundary in a distinct ledger.
guardrail: Define each validation error and canonical array index as an own enumerable data property with Object.defineProperty. Verify invalid admission, direct digest rejection, unchanged baseline digests, distinct high-index digest identity and append CONFLICT under reversible inherited numeric setters. Never treat the tests as proof of independent settlement authenticity.
